intro: Match each piece of evidence to what it means.

left.label: The Stamp Act Congress says only the colonists' own representatives can tax them.
Under the Articles, any change needed every state to agree.
The three-fifths clause counted enslaved people for seats but gave them no vote.
Washington writes that the nation is “fast heading toward anarchy.”
The Sedition Act jailed editors who criticized the president.

right.label: …which means Parliament's tax broke a right the colonists believed they already had.
…which means one state could block any change to the Articles.
…which means slaveholding states gained power in Congress from people who had no say.
…which means even the country's most trusted leader thought the Articles were failing.
…which means the First Amendment's promise was tested only seven years after it was made.

rationale.a: The evidence is the claim; the explanation is why it mattered: a right taken away.
rationale.b: Article XIII required every state legislature to agree, so a single state held a veto.
rationale.c: More seats for the South, counted from people who could not vote.
rationale.d: It matters who said it: the hero of the Revolution was scared.
rationale.e: 1791 to 1798: the promise of free speech and press was tested fast.

a: What did the colonists believe they already had?
b: If everyone has to agree, what can one “no” do?
d: Why does it matter that Washington said it?
e: When was the First Amendment ratified?
